theme: No condemnation; the Spirit; nothing separates us
readingInstruction: Read Romans 8:1-39. Many Christians call this the greatest chapter in the Bible. Read it slowly, perhaps in two sittings: verses 1-17 on life in the Spirit, and verses 18-39 on suffering, glory, and the love of God.
settingTheScene: Chapter 7 ended with the cry “Wretched man that I am!” Chapter 8 begins with the answer: no condemnation. The Holy Spirit, mentioned only a few times in the first seven chapters, appears nearly twenty times here. The chapter moves from the Spirit’s work within, to the groaning of creation, to the unbreakable love of God. It is a summit of the Bible, and many believers have memorized it.
observation: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus” (8:1).
“You, however, are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you” (8:9).
“For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, Abba! Father!” (8:15).
“For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us” (8:18).
“And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose” (8:28).
“If God is for us, who can be against us?” (8:31).
“He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him graciously give us all things?” (8:32).
“Nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord” (8:39).
interpretation:
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” The word “now” is emphatic: the verdict is already given. The reason: “the law of the Spirit of life has set you free in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and death.” What the law could not do, weakened by the flesh, God did: by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh. The condemnation fell on Christ so that none falls on us. And the result is that the righteous requirement of the law is fulfilled in us, who walk according to the Spirit.

Verses 5 to 11 contrast two ways of living: the mind set on the flesh is death, and the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace. Every Christian has the Spirit: “Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him.” And the Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead will give life to our mortal bodies. The resurrection is already at work in us.

Verses 12 to 17 speak of adoption. We are not debtors to the flesh. By the Spirit we put to death the deeds of the body. All who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. The Spirit does not make us fearful slaves but sons who cry “Abba! Father!” (an Aramaic word of intimate address). The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs, fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him.

Verses 18 to 27 deal with suffering. The present sufferings are not worth comparing with the coming glory. Creation itself waits with eager longing, subjected to futility, groaning as in the pains of childbirth. We also groan, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our bodies. “In this hope we were saved.” And the Spirit helps us in our weakness: “We do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.”

Then the golden chain. “We know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose.” This is not that all things are good, but that God works all things for the good of his people, and the good is defined in verse 29: to be conformed to the image of his Son. “For those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son… and those whom he predestined he also called, and those whom he called he also justified, and those whom he justified he also glorified.” Notice that the chain has no broken links. Everyone who is justified will be glorified. Christians differ about the meaning of “foreknew”: Reformed readers hold that it means God set his love on them beforehand, while others hold that it refers to God’s foreknowledge of their faith. All agree that salvation is secured by God’s purpose.

Paul ends with a series of questions that no one can answer against us. “If God is for us, who can be against us?” “He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him graciously give us all things?” “Who shall bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.” “Who is to condemn? Christ Jesus is the one who died, more than that, who was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who indeed is interceding for us.” “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?” Not tribulation, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, or sword. “In all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.” And the closing: “neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers, nor height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
connection: Romans 5:1-11 anticipates the confidence of this chapter. John 14:15-17 and 16:7-15 promise the Spirit. Galatians 4:4-7 also speaks of the Spirit of adoption. Genesis 3:17-19 explains why creation groans. Isaiah 65:17-25 and Revelation 21:1-5 promise a new creation. Ephesians 1:3-14 speaks of election and the Spirit as a seal. Philippians 1:6 and John 10:28-29 assure perseverance. Psalm 44:22 is quoted in verse 36. Hebrews 7:25 says Christ always lives to make intercession for us. 1 John 4:9-10 speaks of God’s love in sending his Son.
application:
Read verse 1 aloud, and put your name in it: there is now no condemnation for me.

Name a present suffering. Compare it to the glory to come, as Paul does, without minimizing the pain.

Memorize verses 38 and 39. Say them when you wake in the night.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that there is now no condemnation for you in Christ.
Thank him for the Spirit of adoption who lets you cry, “Abba, Father.”
Tell him what you want to be sure cannot separate you from his love.
